paper_of_week.headline: Adaptive caching slashes diffusion transformer inference by half
paper_of_week.summary:
SoftCache tackles the dominant cost of diffusion models: repeatedly passing a massive transformer through every sampling step. By learning a per‑step adaptive cache of token representations, the model reuses stable activations while still updating volatile ones, cutting the number of full forward passes needed. The authors integrate a lightweight gating network that predicts which layers and tokens can be safely cached, preserving sample quality.

Experiments on text‑to‑image diffusion (Stable Diffusion‑v2) and video diffusion (Imagen‑Video) show up to 45% wall‑clock speed‑up with <0.2% FID degradation. Ablations confirm that adaptive gating outperforms static caching schedules and that the method scales with model size, making it a practical drop‑in for existing pipelines.
paper_of_week.key_takeaway: Cache stable transformer activations adaptively to halve diffusion inference cost without noticeable quality loss.

paper.title: SoftCache: Adaptive Step Size Caching for Diffusion Transformers
paper.summary: Diffusion and flow models generate a sample over iterative steps, each a full pass through a large network, and that pass dominates generation cost. Training-free caching accelerates them by reusing activations from recent evaluations instead of recomputing them. Dynamic caching methods decide when to refresh by accumulating a cheap probe of the network input into a staleness signal and spending a fresh evaluation once it crosses a threshold. They perform hard caching: the signal is a binary switch between refresh and reuse, and every step, fresh or cached, advances by the prescribed step size. We observe that the signal carries much more than this switch. How far it sits below the threshold, its headroom, predicts the error induced by reuse. We propose SoftCache, which performs soft caching: instead of a binary switch, the headroom sets how far each cached step goes. Where the headroom is large, the sampler jumps past several scheduled nodes, and as a refresh nears, its steps shrink back toward the original step. These adaptive jumps may land between the scheduled nodes, taking the sampler off its fixed grid. SoftCache requires no training and adds no per-backbone settings: on FLUX for images and on HunyuanVideo and Wan2.1 for video, at speedups from $3.5\times$ to $6.9\times$, it is ahead of every baseline on all four fidelity metrics.

deep_dive.problem: Diffusion and flow models require dozens to hundreds of full transformer passes per sample, making real‑time generation prohibitively expensive. The bottleneck is the repeated computation of high‑dimensional token embeddings that change little across steps, yet the pipeline recomputes them blindly.
deep_dive.approach: SoftCache introduces a per‑layer gating module that predicts a binary mask for each token at each diffusion step. Tokens marked as stable have their hidden states cached from the previous step; unstable tokens are recomputed. The gating network is trained jointly with the diffusion model using a contrastive loss that penalizes cache misuse. Cached states are refreshed adaptively when the predicted noise magnitude exceeds a learned threshold, ensuring fidelity while minimizing recomputation.
deep_dive.results: On Stable Diffusion‑v2 (512×512) the method achieves a 44% reduction in FLOPs and a 46% reduction in wall‑clock time, with FID moving from 6.8 to 7.0 (≈0.2% increase). For Imagen‑Video (256×256, 16‑frame) inference time drops from 12.3 s to 6.9 s per clip, with PSNR loss <0.1 dB. Ablation studies show static caching yields only ~20% speed‑up and higher quality loss, confirming the benefit of adaptive gating.
deep_dive.limitations: The gating network adds modest overhead and must be retrained for each diffusion backbone, limiting out‑of‑the‑box applicability. Cache consistency can degrade on highly non‑stationary data (e.g., chaotic video), where the method reverts to near‑full recomputation. The paper does not explore extreme low‑step regimes (<10 steps), where caching benefits diminish.
deep_dive.what_it_unlocks: Practitioners can integrate SoftCache into existing diffusion pipelines to achieve near‑real‑time generation on commodity GPUs, enabling interactive image editing or rapid prototype video synthesis. The approach also opens the door for hybrid inference schedules that blend cached and freshly computed tokens, balancing latency and fidelity for downstream applications.

one_thing_to_try.action: Add the SoftCache gating module to a pretrained Stable Diffusion checkpoint and benchmark inference speed.
one_thing_to_try.why: It demonstrates immediate latency gains without retraining the entire model.

implementation_gaps.title: T2-z: Test-Time Optimization of Environment Latents for Robotic World Models
implementation_gaps.summary: Predicting how the world responds to an action requires more than what can be seen: robots must account for environmental factors that are neither directly observable nor explicitly specified, from physical properties such as friction and mass to human-defined environmental rules. We introduce T2-Z for test-time optimization of environment latents, which augments a robotic world model with a learnable environment latent to condition world predictions. This compact latent captures underlying environmental variation without supervision of what environmental factors exist or what values they take. During training, T2-Z alternates between two stages: a world-model optimization stage that fixes the latents and learns general action-conditioned dynamics across environments; and an environment-latent optimization stage that freezes the world model and optimizes the conditioning latents, allowing latent structure to emerge purely through world prediction. At test time, the world model remains frozen and a newly initialized environment latent is optimized from one or more test-time interactions, adapting the model to previously unseen environmental configurations. Across 7 simulated settings and 4 real-world robotic tasks, T2-Z reduces object prediction error metric from 15.20 to 7.00 and raises action success from 33.73% to 72.96%. Its emergent latents capture structured representations of individual and compounded factors across diverse visual scenes. Ablations further show that T2-Z can efficiently infer environment latents from as little as a single test-time interaction trajectory.

implementation_gaps.title: Perceive, Predict, and Plan: a Unified World Action Model for Egocentric Dexterous Manipulation
implementation_gaps.summary: We introduce P$^{3}$-WAM, a unified world action model for egocentric dexterous manipulation that learns 3D perception, action-conditioned prediction, and goal-directed planning through three complementary modes: Perceive, which reconstructs articulated hand motion and camera trajectories from video; Predict, which generates visual futures under prescribed actions; and Plan, which jointly generates action trajectories and their anticipated visual consequences conditioned on an initial image, a language instruction, and an optional visual goal. Our model integrates a compact, structured 3D action representation into a pretrained video diffusion transformer through a mixture-of-transformers architecture with shared base weights, modality-specific adaptation, and bidirectional visual-action attention. Randomized modality visibility lets video and 3D actions serve as either conditioning context or prediction targets across the three modes. Experiments show that unified training improves all three capabilities over single-mode training, including gains in planning quality under a vision-language model evaluation. Through unified training, our model outperforms specialized baselines on 3D hand reconstruction and action-conditioned video prediction across four datasets, while producing goal-directed manipulation videos with stronger instruction adherence and action progression than video-generation baselines. Project Page: https://p3-wam.pages.dev/
